title: Top-k retrieval degradation is a marginal-information trade-off, not a new self-evolution primitive
dead_end_scope: The standalone claim that GeoForge's slight trajectory-quality degradation under excessive skill retrieval and its optimum near Top-k=3 / Min-Retrieve-Score=0.6 identify a new agent-specific self-evolution mechanism merely from the nonmonotonic retrieval curve.

counter_explanation.statement: GeoForge itself attributes the sensitivity curve to the ordinary quality-coverage trade-off of retrieved guidance: a small number of high-quality skills performs best, excessive retrieval slightly degrades trajectory quality because guidance becomes redundant, and an overly strict score threshold hurts Tool-Exact-Match by filtering useful experiences. This is exactly the prediction of marginal-information/complementarity-versus-redundancy models under a finite context/action-planning budget. The system's own mature reduction ledger likewise treats sharing-helpful versus sharing-collapse behavior as information redundancy/correlation or diversity-consensus trade-off unless a same-information residual survives.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: With the retrieval scoring function, candidate skill pool, context/token budget, and downstream planner fixed, increasing k should initially add useful complementary information, then yield diminishing marginal value as lower-ranked skills become redundant, weakly relevant, or conflicting; raising the score threshold should remove noise until it begins discarding useful evidence. A nonmonotonic optimum in k or threshold is therefore expected without introducing a new self-evolution object.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: Retrieval utility depends on marginal complementary information under a finite planning/context budget; more retrieved skills are not monotonically better when lower-ranked guidance is redundant or conflicting.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Search only for matched retrieval sets with the same relevance scores, token/context budget, redundancy/complementarity statistics, skill count, and planner information where an agent-specific structural variable still predicts a different ex-ante trajectory or task outcome. Require same-information redundancy/correlation, submodular-diversity, retrieval-utilization, and negative-transfer baselines to fail. Do not reopen from another Top-k optimum or another observation that more context can hurt.
counter_explanation.scope: GeoForge arXiv:2608.10494v1 sensitivity analysis over the number of retrieved skills and minimum retrieval-score threshold, including the reported Top-k=3 and Min-Retrieve-Score=0.6 operating point.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: The degradation reflects an unexplained optimizer instability: the paper explicitly attributes it to redundant guidance under excessive retrieval.

The optimum is caused only by a strict filtering failure: the two sweeps have opposite sides of the same quality-coverage trade-off—too much low-marginal-value guidance versus filtering useful experiences.

The effect requires a geospatial-specific causal object: the stated mechanism depends on relevance, redundancy, retrieval count, and planning quality, all directly expressible by generic marginal-information and negative-transfer models.

A new self-evolution mechanism follows because the retrieved objects are evolved skills: evolution determines the available artifacts, but the reported sensitivity experiment varies retrieval hyperparameters over the resulting library; the observed Top-k nonmonotonicity is a retrieval-selection phenomenon.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only if a preregistered matched comparison equalizes retrieved-skill count, relevance/score profile, context/token budget, pairwise redundancy/complementarity, planner/backbone, and observable retrieval-utilization information, yet a self-evolution-specific structural variable produces a distinct ex-ante trajectory-quality or task-utility prediction that same-information redundancy/correlation, submodular-diversity, negative-transfer, and retrieval-utilization models cannot express. A new k, threshold, domain, or retrieval curve is insufficient.

do_not_say: structured skill memory has no value
scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: GeoForge provides a clean quantitative example that retrieval quality is nonmonotonic in quantity, but its own explanation and same-information mature theory already identify the governing object as marginal useful information versus redundant guidance.
